concern: Apparatus and methods for controlled clot aspiration — CEO-identified adjacent art
title: Apparatus and methods for controlled clot aspiration
claims: Claims ( 13 ) A vacuum aspiration control system for use with a vacuum source (700) and an aspiration catheter (750, 751), said system comprising: a connecting tube (206, 706) configured to connect the vacuum source with the aspiration catheter or component thereof; an on-off valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) configured to be operatively coupled to the connecting tube; a sensing unit (224, 246, 282, 284) configured to detect flow within the connecting tube and to produce a signal representative of such flow; and a controller (220) configured to receive the signal representative of flow through the connecting tube and to open and close the on-off valve, wherein the controller is configured to automatically close the valve to stop flow through the connecting tube when the signal indicates unrestricted flow. A vacuum aspiration control system as in claim 1, wherein the controller (220) closes the valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) when unrestricted flow is detected and periodically opens the valve for a time interval to sample flow, wherein the valve is closed again if unrestricted flow is detected and the valve is held open if unrestricted flow is not detected. A vacuum aspiration control system as in claim 2, wherein the controller (220) includes a sampling delay between closing the valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) for unrestricted flow and opening the valve to sample flow; optionally, wherein the sampling delay progressively changes in duration when unrestricted flow continues to be detected; and/or optionally, wherein the sampling delay increases in duration with each consecutive reading of unrestricted flow. A vacuum aspiration control system as in claim 2, wherein the flow is sampled and a new valve position is determined in a millisecond time frame. A vacuum aspiration control system as in claim 1, wherein the connecting tube (206, 706) is linear in an unconstrained configuration, with a first end configured for attachment to the vacuum source (700), or component thereof, and a second end configured for attached to the aspiration catheter (750, 751), or component thereof; and/or wherein the sensing unit (224, 246, 282, 284) comprises any one or more of differential pressure sensors, magnetic flow sensors, acoustic flow sensors, optical flow sensors, thermal flow sensors, and sensors to detect circumferential expansion/contraction of the connecting tube; and/or wherein the sensing unit comprises a pair of pressure sensors disposed along the connecting tube to measure differential pressure; and/or wherein the on-off valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) comprises a solenoid actuator comprised of a pinch valve or an angle valve that is powered to open the valve. A vacuum aspiration system as in claim 1, wherein the controller (220) is configured to open the valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) and hold the valve open until unrestricted flow is detected whereupon the controller closes the valve; and/or wherein the controller closes the valve when the signal indicates unrestricted flow, periodically opens the valve for a time interval to sample flow, and holds the valve open when the signal indicates flow is no longer unrestricted; and/or wherein the controller closes the valve when unrestricted flow is detected and periodically opens the valve for a time interval to sample flow and determine a new valve position, wherein the new valve position is closed if flow is still unrestricted and the new valve position is open if flow is no longer unrestricted; and/or wherein the controller initiates a sampling mode when the signal indicates unrestricted flow, wherein the valve is closed and periodically opened for a time interval to sample flow, wherein the sampling mode ends when the signal indicates that sampled flow is no longer unrestricted; and/or wherein the controller is configured to automatically close the valve to stop flow through the connecting tube (206, 706) when the signal indicates unrestricted flow and the controller periodically tests flow by opening the valve for a time interval to establish a test flow and to resume a treatment flow if the test flow is no longer unrestricted. A vacuum aspiration system as in claim 1, wherein the controller (220) is configured to allow a user to manually open the valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) until unrestricted flow is detected whereupon the controller closes the valve; optionally, further comprising a manual switch in communication with the controller to allow a user to manually open the valve. A vacuum aspiration system as in claim 1, wherein the system comprises a base unit which incorporates at least the on-off valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) and the controller (220); optionally, wherein the connecting tube (206, 706) has a proximal end configured to connect to the vacuum source (700) and a distal end configured to connect to the aspiration lumen in the aspiration catheter (750, 751), said system further comprising an external unit (204, 204a) configured to be secured to the connecting tube at a location between the distal end and the proximal end thereof; optionally, wherein the external unit comprises at least a portion of the sensing unit (224, 246, 282, 284); optionally, wherein the sensing unit comprises a first pressure sensor in the base unit and a second pressure sensor in the external unit, wherein the controller is configured to determine a differential pressure based on signals from the first and second pressure sensors. A vacuum aspiration control system, in particular according to any of claims 1 to 8, for use with a vacuum source (700) and an aspiration catheter (750, 751), said system comprising: a connecting tube (206, 706) configured to connect the vacuum source with an aspiration lumen in the aspiration catheter; an on-off valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) configured to be operatively coupled to the connecting tube; a sensing unit (224, 246, 282, 284) configured to detect flow within the connecting tube and to produce a signal representative of such flow; and a controller (220) connected to receive the signal representative of flow through the connecting tube and to open and close the on-off valve, wherein the controller is configured to automatically close the valve to stop flow through the connecting tube when the signal indicates the catheter is aspirating blood free of vessel-obstructing clot. A vacuum aspiration system as in claim 9, wherein the controller (220) is further configured to automatically open the valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) to sample flow through the connecting tube (206, 706) and remain open when the signal indicates that the catheter (750, 751) is aspirating blood having vessel-obstructing clot; and/or wherein the controller (220) is configured to open the valve and hold the valve open until the controller receives a signal indicating that the aspiration catheter is aspirating blood free of vessel-obstructing clot, whereupon the controller closes the valve. A vacuum aspiration system as in claim 9, wherein the controller (220) is configured to periodically open a closed on-off valve (228, 286, 296, 396, 496, 499, 550, 796, 799) to receive a new signal representative of flow to determine whether the on-off valve should remain closed; optionally, wherein the controller includes a sampling delay between closing the valve when the signal indicates the catheter (750, 751) has aspirated blood free of vessel-obstructing clot and opening the valve to sample flow; optionally, wherein the sampling delay increases in duration with each consecutive signal indicating that the catheter has been positioned in clot-free blood.
